title: Seeds on the Move: Parent Guide
endLine: Seed shapes carry seeds away by wind, water and animals.

scenes.tts: A plant can't walk. So how do its seeds get to new places? An old fuzzy sock pulled over your shoe can catch some in the act.
scenes.caption: A plant can't walk. So how do its seeds get to new places? An old fuzzy sock pulled over your shoe can catch some in the act.
scenes.visual: Friendly schematic: a sunny weedy edge of a yard with tall seed heads swaying. A single shoe with an old fuzzy sock pulled over it steps into the frame. Large text: 'How do seeds travel?' No photos of real children.
scenes.narration: A plant can't walk. So how do its seeds get to new places? An old fuzzy sock pulled over your shoe can catch some in the act.

scenes.visual: Same weedy edge; the sock-covered shoe pauses. Title 'Seeds on the Move' appears for 2 seconds while seed heads sway.

scenes.tts: In about thirty-five minutes, your child practices looking closely, sorting by a rule, and testing a guess. They notice how seed shapes help seeds travel by wind, water, and animals, including people.
scenes.caption: In about thirty-five minutes, your child practices looking closely, sorting by a rule, and testing a guess. They notice how seed shapes help seeds travel by wind, water, and animals, including people.
scenes.visual: The view widens: four small icons rise above the weeds one by one, a winged seed with wind lines, a seed on a ripple, a hooked burr on a sock, and a berry beside a bird. Labels: 'Wind', 'Water', 'Animals', 'People'.
scenes.narration: In about thirty-five minutes, your child practices looking closely, sorting by a rule, and testing a guess. They notice how seed shapes help seeds travel by wind, water, and animals, including people.

scenes.tts: Ask, 'How do seeds get to new places?' Write down their ideas. Slip the sock over one shoe. Walk slowly along the weedy edge for three to five minutes. Collect only seeds you know are safe to handle, like maple keys.
scenes.caption: Ask, 'How do seeds get to new places?' Write down their ideas. Slip the sock over one shoe. Walk slowly along the weedy edge for three to five minutes. Collect only seeds you know are safe to handle, like maple keys.
scenes.visual: Show the question in a speech bubble beside a sheet for predictions. Show the sock-covered shoe brushing the seed heads along the edge while a timer reads '3 to 5 min'. On the way back, an adult puts a fallen maple key in a paper bag.
scenes.narration: Ask, 'How do seeds get to new places?' Write down their ideas. Slip the sock over one shoe. Walk slowly along the weedy edge for three to five minutes. Collect only seeds you know are safe to handle, like maple keys.

scenes.tts: Stay outdoors to check the sock. Lay it on white paper. You pull off what stuck with tweezers, looking for ticks as you go. Then seal the sock in a zip-top bag.
scenes.caption: Stay outdoors to check the sock. Lay it on white paper. You pull off what stuck with tweezers, looking for ticks as you go. Then seal the sock in a zip-top bag.
scenes.visual: On an outdoor step, the sock lies on white paper. An adult hand with tweezers lifts burrs one at a time onto the paper. A small magnifier circle sweeps across the sock, marked 'Look for ticks'. Then the sock slides into a zip-top bag that seals.
scenes.narration: Stay outdoors to check the sock. Lay it on white paper. You pull off what stuck with tweezers, looking for ticks as you go. Then seal the sock in a zip-top bag.

scenes.tts: Use a hand lens to see how hooks and spines caught on the sock. Then make four piles: flies, floats, sticks, gets eaten. Ask, 'Why does this one go in that pile?' Some seeds fit two piles, and that is fine.
scenes.caption: Use a hand lens to see how hooks and spines caught on the sock. Then make four piles: flies, floats, sticks, gets eaten. Ask, 'Why does this one go in that pile?' Some seeds fit two piles, and that is fine.
scenes.visual: A magnified circle shows a burr's tiny hooks gripping sock fibres. The seeds then slide into four labelled piles on the table: Flies, Floats, Sticks, Gets eaten. One seed hovers between two piles with a small smile icon.
scenes.narration: Use a hand lens to see how hooks and spines caught on the sock. Then make four piles: flies, floats, sticks, gets eaten. Ask, 'Why does this one go in that pile?' Some seeds fit two piles, and that is fine.

scenes.tts: Stay with your child at a shallow bowl of water. Ask which seeds will float. Drop one of each kind into the water. Check again after ten minutes. Empty the bowl when you're done.
scenes.caption: Stay with your child at a shallow bowl of water. Ask which seeds will float. Drop one of each kind into the water. Check again after ten minutes. Empty the bowl when you're done.
scenes.visual: Show an adult beside a child at the table, with only enough water in the bowl to float the seeds. Seeds drop in, and a clock reads '10 minutes later'. The adult empties the bowl at the end.
scenes.narration: Stay with your child at a shallow bowl of water. Ask which seeds will float. Drop one of each kind into the water. Check again after ten minutes. Empty the bowl when you're done.

scenes.tts: Now a question for you. Stand on the floor and hold a whole maple key up high. Snap the wing off another key. Hold both at the same height. Which do you predict will land first?
scenes.caption: Now a question for you. Stand on the floor and hold a whole maple key up high. Snap the wing off another key. Hold both at the same height. Which do you predict will land first?
scenes.visual: A whole maple key and a wingless seed part are held at the same height by two schematic hands, side by side. A dashed line marks the drop height. Large question card at left: 'Which lands first?'
scenes.narration: Now a question for you. Stand on the floor and hold a whole maple key up high. Snap the wing off another key. Hold both at the same height. Which do you predict will land first?

scenes.visual: Hold the two raised seeds and the question card. Subtle motion: the whole key's wing trembles slightly in still air; nothing drops yet.

scenes.tts: The key without its wing hits the floor much sooner. The whole key spins as it falls, and the spinning wing slows its drop. A breeze then has more time to push it sideways. Time three drops of each.
scenes.caption: The key without its wing hits the floor much sooner. The whole key spins as it falls, and the spinning wing slows its drop. A breeze then has more time to push it sideways. Time three drops of each.
scenes.visual: Both seeds release in still air. Show the wingless seed landing first while the whole key spins down. Mark the stopwatch comparison 'schematic'. After the comparison, replay the whole key falling with a breeze arrow pushing it sideways.
scenes.narration: The key without its wing hits the floor much sooner. The whole key spins as it falls, and the spinning wing slows its drop. A breeze then has more time to push it sideways. Time three drops of each.

scenes.tts: Choose a patch where picking is allowed. Stay within arm's reach outdoors. Never taste any part of a wild plant. Keep acorns, small seeds, and burrs away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. If anyone swallows berries or seeds from the activity, call Poison Help.
scenes.caption: Choose a patch where picking is allowed. Stay within arm's reach outdoors. Never taste any part of a wild plant. Keep acorns, small seeds, and burrs away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. If anyone swallows berries or seeds from the activity, call Poison Help.
scenes.visual: Back at the weedy edge, show an adult and child close together. Use three safety marks: a wild plant crossed out at a mouth, small seeds and burrs beside 'Under 4: choking risk', and a phone reading 'Choking: 911 first'.
scenes.narration: Choose a patch where picking is allowed. Stay within arm's reach outdoors. Never taste any part of a wild plant. Keep acorns, small seeds, and burrs away from children under four. Call nine one one if choking. If anyone swallows berries or seeds from the activity, call Poison Help.

scenes.tts: Ticks live in tall grass. Wear closed shoes and tuck long pants into socks. Before going inside, check your child's skin, scalp, hair, and clothes for ticks. Wash hands with soap after handling seeds.
scenes.caption: Ticks live in tall grass. Wear closed shoes and tuck long pants into socks. Before going inside, check your child's skin, scalp, hair, and clothes for ticks. Wash hands with soap after handling seeds.
scenes.visual: At the same weedy edge, show long pants tucked into socks above closed shoes. A magnifier checks the child's head, exposed skin, and clothes. End on soapy hands under a tap.
scenes.narration: Ticks live in tall grass. Wear closed shoes and tuck long pants into socks. Before going inside, check your child's skin, scalp, hair, and clothes for ticks. Wash hands with soap after handling seeds.

scenes.tts: Look back at your child's first ideas. Ask, 'How did the seeds on the sock get there?' Any seeds that stuck show how people can carry them. If the sock stayed empty, try again later.
scenes.caption: Look back at your child's first ideas. Ask, 'How did the seeds on the sock get there?' Any seeds that stuck show how people can carry them. If the sock stayed empty, try again later.
scenes.visual: Bring back the prediction sheet beside the white paper with the seeds removed from the sock. Show a hook catching on a sock fiber, then show the shoe carrying the seed along the path.
scenes.narration: Look back at your child's first ideas. Ask, 'How did the seeds on the sock get there?' Any seeds that stuck show how people can carry them. If the sock stayed empty, try again later.

scenes.visual: End card over the weedy edge, with the spinning maple key, a hooked burr and a fluffy seed drifting in the background. Large centered text: 'Seed shapes carry seeds away by wind, water and animals.'
scenes.line: Seed shapes carry seeds away by wind, water and animals.
